findings.text: The parman selftest provides load and unload hooks. Load runs a sorting validation cycle and reports its outcome, while unload carries no teardown action. The cycle owns a transient test handle that is always released before returning. Identifiers involved include test_parman_init, test_parman_exit and test_parman_lsort.

Priority array acceptance requires positional identity between stored index and slot position, equality between locally counted live entries and the stored live total, and trailing idle capacity strictly below the configured resize step. Any breach is reported as invalid input with an informational success signal otherwise. Identifiers involved include index, used_items and last_unused_items.

Sort validation gates verification on successful execution, with creation failure propagating directly and destruction following any successful creation. Verification itself combines ordering, count and capacity checks. Identifier involved includes test_parman_lsort.

Mismatched placement, count divergence and excessive trailing idle space each cause the validation to fail as invalid input rather than proceeding. Execution and verification errors propagate to the caller after releasing the test handle, preventing use of an unchecked structure.

The ref tracker selftest holds a single directory object plus a fixed-capacity table of tracker pointers. Each slot is independently addressable for allocation and release, supporting distinct call-site tracking per slot. Identifiers involved include ref_dir and tracker.
The tracker pointer table holds 20 [CITED] entries.

Allocation wrappers are generated per index as distinct non-inlineable routines so each test slot produces a separate call site for tracking attribution. All wrappers share the same contract of taking a directory and a slot reference with kernel allocation context. Identifier involved includes TRT_ALLOC.

Timer coordination pairs a timer object with an atomic completion flag initially cleared. The callback combines allocation of the initial tracker slot in atomic context with completion signalling, enabling polling for progress. Identifiers involved include test_ref_tracker_timer, test_ref_timer_done and test_ref_tracker_timer_func.

The ref tracker scenario operates on a bounded named directory with a timer-driven concurrent allocation synchronized through an atomic completion signal. Diagnostic coverage relies on distinct attribution per populated slot, intentional retention of references through teardown, and duplicate release as a warning trigger, with teardown expected to surface the retained items.

The selftest deliberately retains live references and repeats a release on an already freed slot to validate warning paths. Teardown is expected to complain about the retained references, so a quiet teardown would indicate missing diagnostics rather than success.
Module load executes the full ref tracker scenario synchronously and reports success, while unload performs no action. All allocation, timer coordination and teardown occur within the load path.
The test directory is configured with quota 100 [CITED] and name selftest.
The test suite caps total entries at 1000000 [CITED]. Identifier involved includes MAX_ENTRIES.
A sentinel marks insertion failure using the maximum integer value. Identifier involved includes TEST_INSERT_FAIL.
Default entry count for runs is 50000 [CITED]. Identifier involved includes parm_entries.
Default serial repetition count is 4 [CITED]. Identifier involved includes runs.
Default maximum table size control is 0 [CITED], selecting automatic sizing. Identifier involved includes max_size.
Automatic shrinking is disabled by default. Identifier involved includes shrinking.
Default element hint is 8 [CITED]. Identifier involved includes size.
Default concurrent worker count is 10 [CITED]. Identifier involved includes tcount.
Retry on memory exhaustion is disabled by default. Identifier involved includes enomem_retry.

Test values carry a numeric identifier plus a thread tag. Plain objects pair the value with a hash chain node, list objects pair it with a list node, and worker context bundles an entry count, a worker tag, a task reference and an object array. Identifiers involved include test_obj_val, test_obj, test_obj_rhl and thread_data.

The duplicate-test hash reduces the identifier modulo 10 [CITED] to force collisions, while comparison orders by identifier difference with equality meaning match. Identifiers involved include my_hashfn and my_cmpfn.

Table parameters bind the hash node offset, key offset and key length to the test object layout with a generic hash. The duplicate variant additionally binds custom object hash and compare plus a fixed element hint and disables automatic shrinking. Identifiers involved include test_rht_params and test_rht_params_dup.
Duplicate-test parameters carry element hint 128 [CITED] with automatic shrinking off.

Insertion retries while the table reports busy, yielding the processor between attempts. When the memory-retry flag is set, memory exhaustion is treated as retriable and counted separately, otherwise it propagates. Success reports the retry count and failure propagates the terminal error. Identifier involved includes insert_retry.

Lookup validation expects even positions to be present and odd positions absent, with the failure sentinel always treated as absent. Present entries must carry matching identifiers, and any deviation is reported as a distinct lookup fault. Identifier involved includes test_rht_lookup.

Lookups and walks run under read-side protection with explicit walk lifecycle of enter, start, iteration, stop and exit. Table dumps take exclusive guard to satisfy checker constraints. Scheduling yields are inserted during long scans. No test-local locks are defined; all guards are external.

Serial hash validation maintains agreement among inserted even keys, traversal accounting and read-guarded lookup outcomes, with removal predicated on prior presence and overall duration reported as elapsed time. Insertion relies on the retry wrapper for busy conditions. Identifiers involved include test_rhashtable, test_bucket_stats and test_rht_lookup.

List-table validation maintains bitmap-tracked membership with presence-conditional expectations for removal and insertion across deterministic and randomized operation mixes. Absent removal must report missing entry, duplicate insertion of an already tracked slot is treated as faulty, and successful operations update the bitmap accordingly. Identifiers involved include test_rhltable and rhlt.

Traversal tolerates resize restarts but warns on walk errors and on divergence between walked count, stored element count and expected entries. Lookup faults for missing, unexpected or mismatched values are treated as test failures. Resize encounters are counted as table jumps.

Capacity enforcement requires that insertion beyond the configured maximum fails with too-big error, while filling up to the limit succeeds. Any other outcome indicates broken limit handling. Identifier involved includes test_rhashtable_max.

Duplicate handling is exercised with colliding identifiers and true duplicates through both fast and slow insertion paths, verifying via table dump that the counted elements match the inserted total. Mismatches are reported as warnings. Identifiers involved include test_insert_dup, test_insert_duplicates_run and print_ht.

Worker validation requires presence consistent with the failure sentinel plus exact thread and identifier match, counting any deviation. Correctness depends on barrier-synchronized start via a shared counter, sentinel-aware checks, and repeated revalidation across removal phases with parking until stop is requested. Identifiers involved include thread_lookup_test, threadfunc and startup_count.

Concurrent startup uses a shared atomic counter initialized to the worker total, with the last arriver waking the group and all workers waiting for the terminal value before proceeding. Interruption during the wait is treated as a worker error. Identifier involved includes startup_count.

Successor iteration from a null predecessor must visit each element exactly once with all identifiers observed, and querying beyond a missing key must report missing entry. The walk runs under read protection with cleanup coverage for inserted elements and table resources. Identifier involved includes test_rhashtable_next_key.
Successor-iteration test uses 8 [CITED] elements.

Test orchestration derives working entry counts and sizing from configured controls with clamping of invalid requests, and gates concurrent execution on worker demand with serial-only completion when no workers are requested. Coverage spans timing, limit enforcement, duplicate handling and successor iteration within the load path. Identifiers involved include test_rht_init and test_rht_exit.

The suite holds global table instances for plain and list variants reused across serial runs. Initialization and teardown pairing per run prevents cross-run state leakage. Identifiers involved include ht and rhlt.
